title: Unequal request attribution from API proxy multiplexing causes underbilling for mixed-hosted/dedicated tenants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported month-to-month usage underbilling after a regional rollout that enabled HTTP/2 multiplexing on our API proxy for throughput gains. Investigation shows the proxy occasionally attributes multi-stream responses to the wrong upstream session, causing per-request token accounting to be split or dropped when requests traverse mixed-hosted/dedicated routing. This leads to undercounting on customer monthly statements and incorrect quota enforcement for Dedicated tenants. Impacted tenants: mixed routing with long-lived streaming sessions and bursty background embed/collection jobs.

Observed behavior: The proxy accepts a single HTTP/2 connection and multiplexes multiple logical requests. In edge cases during stream rebinds and connection handoff (regional failover/eviction), the attribution header (x-rw-attrib-token) is rewritten or omitted for some streams. The billing pipeline expects one attribution header per logical request. Missing or recomposed headers are either set to a generic fallback tenant ID or discarded, resulting in tokens being excluded from final ledger aggregation.

Why this matters: Customers are seeing underbilled totals (not overbilled) which has legal/contract implications and creates trust issues. For Dedicated customers with committed spend, undercounting also masks capacity pressure and can delay capacity upgrades triggering operational risk.

Scope: Preliminary scan of token ledgers for last 30 days shows ~0.6-1.7% undercount for 12 enterprise tenants (hosted+Dedicates) in NA region during the March 2-8 rollout window. The issue is intermittent and correlates with proxy handshake/connection churn metrics.

Desired outcome: Patch proxy attribution logic to guarantee stable per-request attribution across multiplex and rebind events, reconcile affected customer ledgers, issue corrective billing adjustments, and add permanent monitoring/alerts to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create test tenant with mixed routing: short-hosted API keys and a Dedicated worker pool attached.
2) Open HTTP/2 connection and issue concurrent streaming generation and short-lived embed requests over same connection.
3) Simulate connection rebind by killing underlying TCP connection on proxy (or simulating regional failover).
4) Observe x-rw-attrib-token header presence on upstream requests and inspect collector logs - missing/rewritten headers appear for a subset of streams.
5) Run ledger aggregation for the test tenant and compare against raw token counts emitted by runtime - mismatch indicates attribution loss.
impact_summary: High customer trust impact (enterprise billing), financial undercounting for 12 tenants (estimated $45k in missed recognized usage for March window), potential capacity sizing blindspots for Dedicated pools.
mitigation_taken: 2026-03-10: Disabled HTTP/2 multiplexing feature flag in NA edge for affected proxies (temporary rollback).

2026-03-10: Enabled best-effort request duplication: when attribution header missing, proxy now replicates last-known attribution for same connection as a short-term stopgap (risk: may over-attribute if multiple tenants share a connection).
2026-03-11: Customer success notified top 12 impacted customers; interim statement and manual ledger review offered.
root_cause_hypothesis: Proxy multiplexing code path does not consistently attach or persist the per-logical-request attribution header through connection rebinds and stream handoffs. There is a race between stream teardown and upstream session handshake that causes the header to be emitted to the wrong upstream socket or dropped. The ledger ingestion pipeline treats missing headers as non-billable by design (historical safeguard).
proposed_work: 1) Fix: Ensure attribution is bound to the logical stream metadata (not the connection) and survive rebinds; modify proxy data structures to carry attribution state per stream. (ENG)
2) Fix: Update ledger ingestion to fallback to proxied metadata tags if header missing; mark items as 'attribution-inferred' rather than dropped. (ENG + Billing)
3) Backfill: Reprocess raw runtime token traces for the affected window and produce corrective ledger entries; generate invoices/credits where appropriate. (Billing ops)
4) Monitoring: Add strict alert when >0.1% of tokens are emitted with 'attribution-missing' tag in a 1-hour window. (Observability)
5) E2E test: Add chaos tests simulating connection rebinds in CI to prevent regression. (SRE/QA)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge proxy attribution fix behind feature flag on canary proxies in staging. 2) Run synthetic workload with simulated rebinds for 48h to validate. 3) Gradual rollout to NA edge (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with close monitoring of 'attribution-missing' metric and ledger deltas. 4) Once stable, re-enable HTTP/2 multiplexing and run backfill for affected customers.
qa_criteria: - No increase in 'attribution-missing' after rollout (target <0.01%). - Backfilled ledgers reconcile with runtime token traces within 0.1% for sampled tenants. - Chaos test passes in CI for 1000 simulated rebind events. - Customer success accepts reconciliation plan for affected accounts.
